decisions.rationale: All 212 comparators were reviewed. The anchor is the Assistant Chat consumer boundary for shared platform contracts; the listed FileSafe recovery-control and blocked-authority records are adjacent consumers or owners, not the same authority, lifecycle, state boundary, outcome, and failure contract.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Rendered-preview sandbox requirements are a member security concern under the anchor's broader source-authority and preview/browser trust separation, so their product authority and failure semantics do not coincide.
All 212 comparators were reviewed exhaustively. None addresses selection of the project-focused Kubernetes operational scope, its administrative exclusions, scale boundary, or owning authority.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. The listed records preserve requested/effective visual distinction or label compatibility, but the anchor assigns product-wide panel-command ownership and state rules; shared vocabulary does not align authority and lifecycle.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Runtime-state presentation and GitHub stable-identity lifecycle are plausible neighbors, but neither is the anchor's cross-reference schema gap spanning actor, role, provider, model, and account authority tokens.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. The listed redaction barrier and debug-capture exception share privacy vocabulary, but the anchor governs browser-artifact manifest coverage and failed-redaction handling across artifact kinds, giving it a different state boundary and failure disposition.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Artifact traversal, rendered-input sandboxing, and attachment encoding are adjacent untrusted-input concerns; none owns the anchor's relative-path and source-URL locator constraints or its containment, scheme, host, and credential failure semantics.

All 212 comparators were reviewed exhaustively. No comparator defines the producer principal, workspace ownership, authorization decision, evidence audience, and consumer responsibility missing from this manifest root contract.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. FileSafe blocked-episode restoration, approval-card interaction, and web-session approval races are member or surface-specific neighbors; the anchor owns the shared HITL blocked-episode resolution race, so authority, state scope, outcomes, and failure semantics remain distinct.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Credential snapshots, GUI identity surfaces, and visualizer audit metadata each have privacy-lifecycle gaps, but they concern different records and consumers from durable HITL approval provenance and therefore fail strict authority and state-boundary equivalence.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. FileSafe blocked-decision delegation and GUI permission-policy authority touch the same approval ecosystem, but the anchor is an umbrella assertion covering HITL owner, event, request, provenance, persistence, and compatibility PlanUnits; umbrella/member structure is not merge-equivalent.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Raw debug-capture governance is adjacent to bounded debug grants, but the anchor additionally spans HITL boundary unification, routing, compatibility, transition reports, tray correlation, and grant semantics, so neither authority nor lifecycle matches.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Gate tags, authority misuse, and blocked-action mapping are neighboring gate concerns, but none defines the phase/task/subtask-toggle to package/seam-gate mapping, precedence, deduplication, and non-one-to-one failure behavior owned by the anchor.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Approval revocation caches, identity-surface privacy, and GitHub stable identity are plausible lifecycle neighbors, but the anchor concerns reusable approval-scope keys and cross-context isolation; their authorities and failure boundaries differ.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. The listed FileSafe recovery records consume or project related blocked and approval state, while the anchor is the broader HITL scheduler-wait, recovery-path, action-gating, label, and approval-ladder contract; member relationships do not merge.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Blocked-episode transitions and approval-card or web-session races are related surfaces, but the anchor uniquely owns expiry versus resolution ordering, scheduler wake, authoritative time, restart catch-up, and exactly-once behavior.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Blocked-action eligibility, FileSafe decision delegation, and GUI permission-policy authority are adjacent, but none supplies the anchor's typed composition between shared permission scopes and HITL runtime action families.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Assistant Chat recovery controls and FileSafe blocked-authority delegation are neighboring consumers, but the anchor specifically prohibits ask-flow from owning a local state machine and routes it through shared approval state; the records do not share authority or full lifecycle.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Destructive approval actions and blocked-decision authority are cases inside the broader decision ecosystem, but neither defines the anchor's bounded classification of auto-resolvable, deferrable, user-authority, and explicit-confirmation uncertainty.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. The listed gate-authority and exemption records are related, but the anchor owns PAUSE-file validation, creator authority, atomicity, race handling, malformed-file fail-safe behavior, audit events, expiry, and exact-action exception precedence.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Approval cards, blocked actions, recovery surfaces, and web-session approval races are consumers or partial lifecycle members; none is the full interoperable HITLRequest wire, version, state-machine, authorization, replay, privacy, delivery, observability, and conformance contract.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. FileSafe destructive-command authority and its approval UI are adjacent controls, but the anchor governs skip and abort runtime commands with run freshness, transactional effects, conflict results, compensation, and audit behavior; related commands are not merge-equivalent.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Card timeout, Assistant Chat recovery, and stale web approval behavior are surface members, while the anchor requires a request-kind timeout action matrix, clock, late/duplicate response handling, delivery recovery, observability, and transition tests across HITL.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Diagnostics, card behavior, recovery controls, responsive accessibility, and account-switch disclosure each overlap one quality dimension, but the anchor is the complete user-visible HITL quality and support envelope; these are adjacent members with different state and failure scopes.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Runtime snapshots, GUI identity surfaces, and GitHub stable identities share privacy or lifecycle concerns, but the anchor is the interview-to-runtime shared identity handoff packet and its consumer-specific classification, redaction, retention, deletion, and observation authorization.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Requested/effective presentation, misleading FileSafe or YOLO state, and account-switch UI testing are plausible display neighbors; the anchor specifically governs summarization of interview-runtime identity and mandatory mismatch and stale-data truth.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Runtime-state distinction, credential-store outages, and account identity lifecycles are neighboring inputs or failures, but none owns the anchor's prelaunch equality and integrity oracle across requested, effective, consumer, and launched-run identity fields.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Blocked episodes and approval recovery surfaces have resolution lifecycles, but the anchor concerns durable interview handoff conflicts, competing values and provenance, blocking scope, authorized resolution, resume persistence, and audit transition; the state objects differ.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Hostile-message validation and operation metadata illustrate adjacent packet concerns, but neither defines the canonical interview handoff field schema, version, referential consistency, trust binding, replay behavior, and validation error codes.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Preview sandboxing, external drag/drop, and closed-by-default library execution are untrusted-input neighbors, but the anchor uniquely governs provider-native import trust, canonical-field precedence, path sanitation, signature checks, quarantine, and import error outcomes.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Visualizer bridge concurrency and backpressure is a plausible concurrency neighbor, but it has a different authority, resource, lifecycle, user outcome, and failure boundary from reviewer-cap reservation, exhaustion, fairness, retry, and cancellation release.

All 212 comparators were reviewed exhaustively. None addresses the documentation-authority contradiction between an implementation-plan title and a body explicitly limited to high-level summary status.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Requested/effective display, adapter conformance, and credential-store outage behavior are neighboring slices, but the anchor is the provider-auth reconciliation invariant across failed, stale, revoked, unavailable, and mismatched requested/effective auth states.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. FileSafe owner boundaries and GUI permission-policy authority are adjacent governance examples, but neither defines conflict precedence, handoff triggers, partial-failure ownership, and consumers across package-local and seam-level governance.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Runtime-state display, identity privacy, credential outages, GitHub identity lifecycle, and account-switch UI are related members; the anchor owns the cross-provider multi-account switch transaction, concurrency, requested/effective history, privacy, failed-switch outcome, and acceptance oracle.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Trusted-daemon revocation, Rust/Slint portability, and transport-path safety touch workbench dependencies, but none is the native workbench service-interface, policy/error, cancellation, trust, and remote-control-loss contract.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Retired-bridge lineage is a neighboring lineage assertion, but it does not define the anchor's predicate for when a historical run becomes lineage-linked to a superseded object, including writer authority, transition, and recovery oracle.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Rendered-preview sandboxing, debug capture, and webview embedding are related technical surfaces, but the anchor owns agent-driven browser navigation authority, untrusted-content isolation, credential/data lifecycle, destructive gating, network loss, capture redaction, and evidence validity.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Approval-card lifecycle, recovery controls, permission-policy ownership, web-session races, and Persona immutability are adjacent members, while the anchor requires the six web operations, batch invariants, approval stages, transition authority, denial behavior, and cross-owner oracle as one falsifiable contract.

All 212 comparators were reviewed exhaustively. None owns Docker registry-management parity, its capability bounds, registry credential lifecycle, destructive confirmations, recovery, scale, and acceptance oracle.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Catalog availability is adjacent to catalog operation, but the anchor is an affirmative authority and merge-precedence contract for a shipped base plus settings overlay keyed by stable IDs; availability failure semantics are a separate lifecycle.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Adapter conformance, catalog availability, and credential-store outage are plausible dependencies, but the anchor owns MCP selection transitions for provider partial availability, connectivity, authentication, tool-identity change, denied enablement, and adapter degradation.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. General file/route identity normalization and owner-derived route normalization are adjacent, but the anchor is the affirmative prohibition against deriving operational target identity from subview or persisted convenience state; authority and outcomes do not fully align.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Adapter conformance and startup validation are related verification concerns, but the anchor specifically distinguishes Doctor metadata registration checks from executing a selected custom tool with timeout, sandbox, exit, side-effect, and evidence-validation oracles.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Execution contexts, redaction barriers, debug capture, identity surfaces, and visualizer audit metadata share privacy dimensions, but the anchor uniquely covers GUI evidence media and manifest-linked artifacts from capture through render, access, retention, deletion, export, consent, capacity, and accessible presentation.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Approval revocation, preview sandboxing, debug capture, and browser-auth shaping are neighboring concerns, but the anchor governs attaching to an existing browser/profile with tab scope, reauthorization, cookie/storage exposure, unrelated-tab exclusion, and detach cleanup.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Projection denial and deliberate authenticated disablement are adjacent gating concepts, but the anchor owns the visible-browser preflight taxonomy separating safe availability fallback from trust, permission, integrity, version, and target-identity failures that must block.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Preview sandboxing, raw debug capture, authenticated authority, and browser-auth shaping are adjacent security mechanisms, but the anchor is the affirmative debug-session rule: ephemeral isolation, attention-required fallback, no unrelated authenticated reuse, and declared-host preflight.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Vision-image permission flow and account-switch UI quality share data or presentation concerns, but the anchor governs mobile screenshot, recording, log, simulator/emulator, and device capture under prompts, personal-data redaction, reset/isolation, degraded network, disconnect recovery, and cleanup.

All 212 comparators were reviewed exhaustively. None concerns the internal normative contradiction over whether Docker Compose gates build and publish actions or is irrelevant to those authoritative action scopes.

All 212 comparators were reviewed. Recovery previews, mutation receipts, and host-side-effect quarantine are analogous recovery mechanisms, but the anchor owns publish and Unraid result payloads, idempotency, retry/resume, digest reconciliation, crash compensation, stale-auth TTL, and partially committed template-repository ownership.
